#01 — Legacy single-step format (backward compatibility) PASS

Old Steps/Expected columns must keep working unchanged after the enhancement.

All 5 legacy rows imported successfully. A step with a missing expected result is skipped with a warning; the testcase itself is still created.

#02 — 0-to-50 step range sweep PASS

One row per step count from 0 through 50 — the core new multi-step feature at scale.

All 51 rows imported successfully. Verified the 0-step and 50-step boundaries directly on the saved testcase pages.

#03 — Steps-only rows (no Expected Result data) PASS

Every Step column filled, every Expected Result column left blank.

Each step is skipped individually with a warning; the testcase is still created using only the core fields.

#04 — Expected-only rows (no Step data) PASS

Mirror of #03 — every Expected Result column filled, every Step column left blank.

Symmetric behavior to #03 confirmed — each expected-result-without-step is skipped cleanly.

#05 — Mixed partial combinations in one file PASS

One file mixing fully-paired rows, steps-only, expected-only, no-step-data, and mid-sequence gaps.

All 6 rows handled independently per their own data; a mid-sequence gap skips only that one step, not the whole case.

#06 — Varying step counts within the same file PASS

Rows with 1, 3, 7, 15, and 30 steps imported together.

No spurious warnings for shorter rows; each row gets exactly its own step count.

#07 — Oversized step text (negative test) PASS

A step field with 2500 characters — over the 2000-char limit.

The entire testcase is rejected on a single oversized step, exactly as documented.

#08 — 2000 / 2001 character boundary PASS

Exact boundary check: a step at exactly 2000 chars (valid) vs. 2001 chars (invalid).

Error message: "Step 1: step content exceeds the maximum length of 2000 characters (got 2001)." Exact validation boundary confirmed.

#09 — Large bulk import PASS

100 test cases x 3 steps each = 300 steps total, imported in a single pass.

Confirms the feature scales well beyond the developer's own 20-case load test.

#10 — Header-only CSV (zero data rows) PASS

A CSV with a valid header row but no data rows at all.

No crash; a clear, actionable error message is shown.

#11 — Completely empty file PASS

A literal 0-byte CSV file.

No crash; a clear, actionable error message is shown.

#12 — Non-sequential step numbering PASS

Header only has Step/Expected Result columns 1, 3, and 5 — skipping 2 and 4.

The importer does not require contiguous step numbering in the source CSV.

#13 — Special characters, unicode, emoji, embedded newlines PASS

Quotes, commas, emoji (🚀), and unicode text (café, naïve, 日本語, тест) in title and step fields, plus a step with an embedded newline.

Verified via raw DOM inspection that unicode text (including the diacritic and Cyrillic case) is stored correctly — an earlier screenshot font-rendering artifact had suggested otherwise; that was a false alarm, corrected after re-checking the actual page text.

#14 — Duplicate "Step 1" header columns BUG FOUND → FIXED & VERIFIED

A malformed CSV where "Step 1" and "Expected Result 1" each appear twice as column headers.

Filed as defect #119818. Fixed by the dev (added the warning banner) and independently retested here — confirmed fixed. Behavior (first occurrence wins) is now clearly communicated instead of silent.

#15 — Header case & whitespace variations BUG FOUND → FIXED & VERIFIED

Column headers with mixed case and stray whitespace: " step 1 " (padded), "EXPECTED RESULT 1" (uppercase), "Step 2" (double-spaced), "expected result 2" (lowercase).

Filed as defect #119817. Fixed by the dev (value lookup now trims whitespace/case consistently) and independently retested twice — confirmed fixed both times.

#16 — Header has Step columns but no Expected Result columns at all PASS

Structural edge case — an entire column family (Expected Result) missing from the header.

No crash on a structurally incomplete header.

#17 — Header has Expected Result columns but no Step columns at all PASS

Mirror of #16 — Step column family entirely missing.

Symmetric behavior to #16 confirmed.
